description: Metformin and iodinated contrast agents increase risk of lactic acidosis
clinical_effect: Lactic acidosis in patients with renal impairment
management: Withhold metformin 48h before and after contrast. Check renal function before restarting.

description: ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics increase risk of hyperkalemia
management: Monitor serum potassium closely. Avoid combination in renal impairment.

description: NSAIDs increase antiplatelet effect and GI bleeding risk with aspirin
management: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for analgesia if patient is on aspirin.

description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, increasing theophylline levels
management: Monitor theophylline levels. Reduce dose by 30-50% or use alternative antibiotic.

description: ACE inhibitors may enhance the hypoglycemic effect of metformin
clinical_effect: Potential for enhanced blood glucose lowering
management: Monitor blood glucose more frequently when initiating or changing dose.

description: Macrolide antibiotics may increase statin exposure via CYP3A4 inhibition
management: Short courses acceptable with monitoring. Watch for muscle pain/weakness.

description: PPIs may reduce the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel via CYP2C19 inhibition
clinical_effect: Reduced clopidogrel efficacy, increased cardiovascular risk
management: Pantoprazole has least interaction. Consider H2 blocker alternative if possible.

description: No clinically significant interaction between amoxicillin-clavulanate and paracetamol
management: No action required. Listed for completeness.

description: Aspirin adds antiplatelet effect on top of warfarin's anticoagulation
clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk including GI and intracranial hemorrhage
management: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated (e.g. mechanical valve). If combined, use lowest effective aspirin dose and monitor INR and for bleeding closely.

description: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and may displace warfarin from plasma proteins, raising INR
management: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for analgesia if patient is on warfarin.

description: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and may displace warfarin from plasma proteins, raising INR
management: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for analgesia if patient is on warfarin.

description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2/CYP3A4 metabolism of warfarin, increasing INR
management: Monitor INR closely for 1-2 weeks after starting or stopping ciprofloxacin.

description: Antibiotics reduce gut-flora vitamin K synthesis and can potentiate warfarin's effect
management: Monitor INR more frequently during and after the antibiotic course.

description: Complex bidirectional interaction: phenytoin can transiently potentiate then, with chronic use, induce warfarin metabolism
management: Monitor INR closely with any phenytoin dose change or on initiation/discontinuation.

description: Loop-diuretic-induced hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia increase the risk of digoxin toxicity
clinical_effect: Digoxin toxicity: arrhythmias, nausea, visual disturbances
management: Monitor serum potassium and magnesium; check digoxin level if toxicity suspected. Consider potassium supplementation.

description: Spironolactone reduces renal clearance of digoxin and may raise serum levels; it can also interfere with some digoxin immunoassays
management: Monitor digoxin levels and for signs of toxicity, especially after dose changes.

description: Loop diuretics reduce renal clearance of lithium
management: Avoid combination if possible; if required, monitor lithium levels closely after initiation or any dose change.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin-mediated clearance of lithium
management: Avoid combination; prefer paracetamol for analgesia. Monitor lithium levels if NSAID use is unavoidable.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin-mediated clearance of lithium
management: Avoid combination; prefer paracetamol for analgesia. Monitor lithium levels if NSAID use is unavoidable.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, raising serum levels
clinical_effect: Increased methotrexate toxicity: myelosuppression, mucositis, hepatotoxicity
management: Avoid concurrent use, particularly around methotrexate dosing days. Monitor blood counts if combination is unavoidable.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, raising serum levels
clinical_effect: Increased methotrexate toxicity: myelosuppression, mucositis, hepatotoxicity
management: Avoid concurrent use, particularly around methotrexate dosing days. Monitor blood counts if combination is unavoidable.

description: Cotrimoxazole (trimethoprim component) has antifolate synergy with methotrexate
management: Avoid combination. If a sulfonamide antibiotic is required, use a non-antifolate alternative.

description: Concurrent nitrate use potentiates PDE5 inhibitors' vasodilatory effect via the nitric oxide/cGMP pathway
management: Absolute contraindication -- do not co-prescribe. Confirm a nitrate-free interval of at least 24h before considering a PDE5 inhibitor.

description: Macrolide antibiotics may increase statin exposure via CYP3A4 inhibition
management: Short courses acceptable with monitoring. Watch for muscle pain/weakness.

description: Omeprazole is a stronger CYP2C19 inhibitor than pantoprazole and more significantly reduces formation of clopidogrel's active metabolite
clinical_effect: Reduced clopidogrel antiplatelet effect, increased cardiovascular risk
management: Prefer pantoprazole or an H2 blocker if PPI co-therapy is needed alongside clopidogrel.

description: Combining an ACE inhibitor and ARB causes dual RAAS blockade
clinical_effect: Increased risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal impairment without added cardiovascular benefit
management: Avoid combination; use a single RAAS-blocking agent.

description: Cotrimoxazole inhibits CYP2C9 and displaces warfarin from plasma protein binding
clinical_effect: Marked INR rise within days, with major bleeding risk
management: Prefer an antibiotic without this interaction. If cotrimoxazole is required, recheck INR within 3 days of starting and again after stopping, and consider a pre-emptive warfarin dose reduction.

description: Clopidogrel adds platelet inhibition on top of warfarin's anticoagulation, with no curated rule between them until now
clinical_effect: Substantially increased major bleeding risk, including GI and intracranial hemorrhage
management: Combine only where both indications are firm (e.g. recent stent with atrial fibrillation), for the shortest duration, and consider gastroprotection. Where combined, monitor INR and for bleeding closely.

description: NSAIDs increase antiplatelet effect and GI bleeding risk with aspirin; ibuprofen additionally blocks aspirin's irreversible COX-1 acetylation and can negate its cardioprotection
clinical_effect: Increased GI bleeding risk, with loss of aspirin's antiplatelet benefit
management: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for analgesia if patient is on aspirin. If an NSAID is unavoidable, dosing it at least 8 hours after the aspirin reduces the competition at COX-1.
